name: Cora Yates
life: “I still remember giving up my chair for an anxious apprentice.” People around the entrance to the Wash House know Cora by a small Friday habit. Cora stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I gave up my slot because I remembered the first day I had nowhere to go before work.
appearance: Cora is easy to recognize by a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape and a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Usually dressed in a dark green knitted vest with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair, Cora draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first when listening.
personality: Cora has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Cora knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To let somebody without elsewhere to go use the slot.
family: Martin Chen is Cora’s older cousin. Cora sets the time to leave. Martin picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The bitter orange*, Martin says, “I delivered bread six mornings a week. On the seventh she ate with my family.”
connections: Gavin Jones. One customer gives up a place and another gets help arriving at an interview.
